correctness.rationale: The one-step height lift is inductively equivalent to the specified Greenberg–Hastings rule and remains 1-Lipschitz. Height ceiling and propagation give the upper bound; the first crossing of the level K-2 gives the lower bound. Uniform color words yield independent centered three-valued increments, so Donsker and Brownian argmax uniqueness squeeze the normalized global extinction time to the transformed arcsine law; boundedness yields the expectation. All configurations n=1..10 and independent integer-encoded n=1..9 were replayed with no disagreement; the finite checks are not used to infer infinite convergence.

originality.rationale: The inspected core published sources prove infinite-volume local one-site decay, 1D general relaxation regimes, and arbitrary-finite-graph synchronization by diameter; their statements do not specify the nondegenerate whole-path global extinction-time limit. The closest published published-finding corpus summary covers the rare endpoint T=n+1 rather than the bulk asymptotic clock. The exact GHM finite-graph walk representation is credited and creates substantial conceptual overlap, but deriving a new distributional consequence requires the near-maximum propagation sandwich and the Brownian argmax theorem. Full access to the later endpoint manuscript and other historical equivalents remains a stated risk.
residual_risks: The nearest later maximal-delay manuscript was inaccessible in complete form; its inaccessible sections might discuss stronger clock distributions.
An unindexed prior asymptotic for finite open-path global extinction could exist.
The proof concerns uniform independent colors only; universality beyond that law has not been established.

value.rationale: A new, natural global-time observable for the standard finite-path excitable system is classified by an explicit nondegenerate arcsine-transformed law, including a sharp asymptotic mean and median. This goes beyond diameter bounds, fixed-site infinite-lattice activity rates, or maximal-delay endpoint counts. The all-size structural sandwich explains the role of spatial extreme positions and makes the result mathematically reusable.
